title: BlueBeacon outbound tactical notebook
body:
Purpose:
Quick working notebook for targeted outbound to BlueBeacon Logistics (regional 3PL). Capture account signals, prioritize outreach sequence, silver-bullet value props, and objection plays. Not for customer-facing distribution — iterative notes + drafts.

Account snapshot (what I can find):
- Name: BlueBeacon Logistics (inc. subsidiaries: BeaconFulfillment LLC)
- HQ: Portland, OR; strong west-coast footprint + 2 regional hubs in TX and GA
- Size: ~420 employees; Series B (2022) — raised to scale fulfillment network
- Tech signals: job postings for "ML Platform Engineer (inference)", public blog post about automating returns processing, uses GCP and has a private VPC in us-west1.
- Triggers: heavy seasonal spikes (Q3-Q4), notes in their engineering blog about "tail latency spikes during peak batches" and manual normalization of conversational returns.

Why Redwood might land here (initial hypothesis):
- Use case alignment: customer support & returns assistant + automated routing of claims to correct teams. Needs low-latency small-context chat + episodic high throughput for batch-processing claims summaries.
- Economics: likely cost sensitivity on per-token for high-volume returns processing and reranking for matching claims to SKUs.
- Compliance: on-prem / VPC deployments plausible because of contractual data controls with retailers.
- Pain to solve: "spiky" throughput, unpredictable latency on busy days, no easy fallback to cheaper models. Redwood can offer Dedicated pools + routing policies + prefix caching to reduce unit cost while keeping latency SLO.

Key contacts (recon):
- CTO (engineering org lead): Daniel Cruz — LinkedIn shows previously at Convoy; speaks about scaling microservices. Likely final decision-maker for infra/vendor fit.
- Head of Ops/Logistics: Priya Menon — cares about operational uptime and SLA guarantees.
- ML Platform owner: Samir Patel (listed in job postings) — will evaluate model runtime, quantization, integration effort.
- Principal Product Manager, Customer Experience: Laura H. — owns feature roadmap for returns UX / agent tooling.

Priority outreach thesis:
1) Low-friction pilot to prove unit economics + SLO behavior during spike (Dedicated small pool + canary routing).
2) Show measurable latency improvement and 30% token-cost delta via batching/caching recommendations (Redwood Optimize).
3) Offer Private deployment evaluation if security controls are gating factor.

Outbound cadence (PRIORITY):
- Touch 1: short intro email from me (Asha) focusing on ops pain and quick pilot concept (3–4 lines).
- Touch 2 (3 days): LinkedIn request + one-liner value prop + 1-pager (convert to PDF: pilot plan, success metrics, rough pricing).
- Touch 3 (1 week): warm call to Samir/Priya for 15 min (tech + ops). Use discovery script below.
- Touch 4: send a short pre-mortem for a hypothetical pilot showing risks and fallbacks (helps get buy-in).

Draft cold email (keep short, test subject variants):
Subject options: "Quick pilot: reduce returns-processing latency at BlueBeacon" / "Small pilot to cut per-claim cost + latency"
Body (variant A):
Hi Priya —
I’m Asha on the infra team at Redwood Inference — we help logistics teams run low-latency LLM features in production (hosted, dedicated, or private). Noticed BlueBeacon has seasonality and notes about latency spikes in claims workflows — we’ve run pilots that cut tail latency by 40% and reduced per-claim compute cost via intelligent batching and prefix caching.
Would you be open to a 15-min intro next week to see if a small dedicated pilot makes sense? I can share a one-page pilot plan with measurable success criteria.
Thanks,
Asha

Quick LinkedIn note (after connect):
Thanks for connecting, Priya — short note: curious if BlueBeacon is exploring production LLMs for returns/customer deflection. We’ve helped fulfillment teams keep latency predictable during peaks. Happy to share a one-pager.

Discovery script / questions (for Samir/Priya call):
- What’s the single biggest pain you see during seasonal peaks? Is it throughput, tail latency, or unexpected error rates?
- How do you currently handle fallback under capacity pressure? Any manual reroutes?
- Have you tried managed LLM endpoints or self-hosted runtimes? What gaps remain?
- What SLA/uptime targets matter to ops and to revenue? (e.g., 99.9% during peak hours?)
- Any data residency or encryption/HSM constraints we should plan for?
- What success metrics would make a pilot an unequivocal win? (e.g., <200ms p50, 95th <800ms, 30% compute cost reduction)

Objection handling (short plays):
- "We already have vendor X / open endpoints": Ask about their pain with tail latency and cost predictability. Position Redwood’s Dedicated + routing policies + fallback models as a reliability layer, not just another API. Offer a short, no-commit benchmark run against their current setup.
- "Security / Data residency concerns": Walk through Private deployment and KMS/HSM support + audit logs. Offer an architecture sketch and a SOC-style checklist.
- "Integration cost / engineering effort": Emphasize SDKs + sample repo, quick start template for returns flow, and a 2-week PoC plan with clear handoffs from Redwood SE.
- "Budget unknown / procurement cycles": Propose a time-boxed evaluation credit and a technical success milestone to justify next budget ask.

Pilot proposal (sketch for one-pager):
- Goal: Demonstrate stable latency under 2x peak load and reduce per-claim compute cost by >=25% without degrading quality for agent suggestions.
- Scope: start with returns summary + routing reranker pipeline (1–2 endpoints) for 500–2,000 daily active claims during pilot window.
- Tech approach: spin a Dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent) routed from canary to fallback cheaper quantized model when queue > threshold; enable prefix/KV caching for repeated SKUs and continuous batching for async claim bulk jobs.
- Success metrics: 95th percentile latency < target, per-claim cost delta, qualitative agent QA score no worse than baseline.
- Timeline: 2 weeks setup (instrumentation + security review) + 4 weeks pilot + 1 week analysis.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Do they have an existing VPC peering process? If yes, procurement time could be 4–6 weeks for Private pilot.
- Confirm what telemetry they can expose: token counts, per-request timings, sample prompts. Need traces for Redwood Console to show improvements.
- What internal stakeholders (legal, procurement) would need an exec summary? Flag for early loop-in.

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize 1-pager + stub pricing for small Dedicated pilot (Marcus & Ivy to help with cost calc).
- Draft short benchmark plan for Samir to run server-side comparison (we provide container + sample workload).
- Sequence warm intro to Priya via mutual contact (Marcus maybe has a PMX connection).
- Prepare a 10-slide light deck: problem, solution, pilot mechanics, expected outcomes, ask.

Notes to self / scratchpad thoughts (raw):
- Try subject line A/B: emphasize latency vs emphasize cost; logistics folks might respond better to "reduce mean time to resolution" language.
- Could pitch retail partner angle: retailers BlueBeacon serves may have SLAs that force transparency on claims turnaround — tie Redwood's reliability story to partner retention.
- If they balk on Dedicated, offer Hosted with strict routing + simulated fallback to show reliability improvements and then propose Dedicated later.

Slack refs / tickets to create:
- #outbound-bluebeacon (create) to centralize assets and convo.
- Ticket: GT-BlueBeacon-pilot (create in Jira) with above timeline / stakeholders.

— end —

(keeping this intentionally conversational — will trim and move to shareable 1-pager when we have a first yes)
